flashcards.q: Why does WHERE ROWNUM <= 5 ORDER BY salary DESC return the WRONG five rows?
flashcards.a: ROWNUM is assigned as rows enter the pre-sort result set -- the limit applies BEFORE the sort, so you get five arbitrary rows presented in salary order. Correct pre-12c: sort in a subquery, filter ROWNUM outside. 12c+: FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY (sorts first by definition).

flashcards.q: Why does WHERE ROWNUM = 2 return nothing?
flashcards.a: ROWNUM is assigned incrementally as rows satisfy predicates: row 2 can't be considered until row 1 is returned, so equality beyond 1 is never satisfiable. Only ROWNUM <= n and ROWNUM = 1 work.

flashcards.q: What does FETCH FIRST bring that ROWNUM cannot do cleanly?
flashcards.a: WITH TIES (include boundary-ranked ties), OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m (pagination -- ROWNUM offset needs double nesting), and sorts-then-limits by construction. ROWNUM-wrap remains for pre-12c estates (11g still runs in production).

flashcards.q: What does Oracle do with empty strings, and what does it silently break?
flashcards.a: '' is treated as NULL: '' IS NULL is TRUE. Breaks: WHERE col <> '' matches nothing, imported MySQL/CSV empty strings behave as NULL, LENGTH('') is NULL not 0. No other major database does this.

flashcards.q: How do NULLs sort by default in Oracle, and how do you fix a DESC report showing NULLs first?
flashcards.a: NULLs are treated as HIGHER than any value: ASC puts them last, DESC puts them FIRST. Fix: ORDER BY salary DESC NULLS LAST. Portable cross-DB pattern: CASE WHEN col IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END trick.

flashcards.q: NVL vs COALESCE -- evaluation, standard, and the DECODE null twist?
flashcards.a: NVL: Oracle-only, evaluates BOTH arguments eagerly. COALESCE: ANSI, lazy per-argument. DECODE: pre-CASE chained equality switch where NULL=NULL MATCHES (a real semantic difference -- NULL = NULL doesn't), but all branches evaluate. New code: ANSI forms.

flashcards.q: Why do sequences have gaps, and when is a gapless requirement legitimate?
flashcards.a: Sequences are not transactional: rollback discards numbers, cache discards on restart -- gaps by design, 'fixing' them by resetting is an anti-pattern. Gapless (invoice numbers) = an accounting requirement solved by serialized counter tables, never sequences.

flashcards.q: What is Oracle's native upsert, and what error signals bad staging data?
flashcards.a: MERGE INTO ... USING ... WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE / WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (no ON CONFLICT -- that's Postgres). ORA-30926 'unable to get a stable set of rows' = multiple staging rows matching one target row: dedupe staging.

flashcards.q: CONNECT BY vs recursive CTE -- which for what?
flashcards.a: CONNECT BY: terse tree walks, LEVEL free, SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH, NOCYCLE for dirty data, zero portability. Recursive CTE (11.2+): ANSI, portable, composable, depth generated manually. New code: CTE; maintenance: read CONNECT BY fluently. Neither is deprecated.

flashcards.q: SYSDATE vs CURRENT_DATE -- what differs for a Tokyo user and a London user?
flashcards.a: SYSDATE = server timezone (both users see the same); CURRENT_DATE = session timezone (calendar dates differ). The bug class is day-boundary logic shifting by session TZ. Fix: store UTC instants (TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE), derive local dates at the edge.

flashcards.q: Why does WHERE date_col BETWEEN SYSDATE-1 AND SYSDATE miss rows from last night?
flashcards.a: Oracle DATE always carries time: SYSDATE is now-with-time, so the range start excludes yesterday-evening rows. The TRUNC habit (or explicit date bounds) is the fix -- the single most common Oracle date bug.

flashcards.q: What is DUAL and why does SELECT 1+1 FROM employees not work?
flashcards.a: DUAL is the one-row scratch table for expression evaluation (Oracle's SELECT historically required FROM). FROM employees returns one row PER employee-row -- DUAL's one-row-ness is the entire point. Modern Oracle special-cases it internally.

flashcards.q: RANK vs DENSE_RANK vs ROW_NUMBER on ties?
flashcards.a: RANK skips after ties (1,1,3), DENSE_RANK doesn't (1,1,2), ROW_NUMBER is unique (1,2,3). Which one 'top 3' wants is the requirement question. 12c optimizer short-circuits ROW_NUMBER Top-N patterns.

flashcards.q: What happens to a tree walk when the data has a cycle, in each form?
flashcards.a: CONNECT BY: ORA-01436 unless NOCYCLE (CONNECT_BY_ISCYCLE flags the rows). Recursive CTE: infinite recursion unless depth-capped in the recursive member. The difference tells an interviewer you've run both against real dirty data.

flashcards.q: What's the career positioning of Oracle dialect depth?
flashcards.a: Consolidation track, not growth: greenfield goes to Postgres/cloud warehouses, but the bank/insurer/healthcare estate pays well precisely because fewer new engineers learn ROWNUM/NVL/DECODE/CONNECT BY. Bilingualism: write ANSI where available, read legacy fluently, always know which the codebase speaks.
